title: इजरायल : विपक्षी नेता गादीलाई सरकार गठन गर्न निम्तो, नेतन्याहुले दिए यस्तो चेतावनी
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । इजरायलका राष्ट्रपति इसाक हर्जोगले विपक्षी नेता गादी आइजेनकोटलाई नयाँ गठबन्धन सरकार गठन गर्ने जिम्मेवारी दिने निर्णय गरेका छन् । गत साता सम्पन्न निर्वाचनमा न त आइजेनकोट नेतृत्वको गठबन्धनले न त प्रधानमन्त्री बेन्जामिन नेतन्याहुको गठबन्धनले सरकार गठनका लागि आवश्यक बहुमत प्राप्त गर्न सके । त्यसपछि राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगले विभिन्न राजनीतिक दलसँग छलफल गरेका थिए । राष्ट्रपतिको निर्णयसँगै आइजेनकोटले नयाँ सरकार गठनका लागि २८ दिनको समय पाएका छन् । आवश्यक परे उनलाई थप १४ दिन समय दिन सकिनेछ । राष्ट्रपतिको निर्णयपछि आइजेनकोटले सामाजिक सञ्जाल एक्समा लेखेका छन्, ‘अब राष्ट्रिय आपत्कालीन सरकार गठन गर्ने समय आएको छ । यसका लागि योग्य बन्न म सक्दो प्रयास गर्नेछु ।’ तर, प्रधानमन्त्री नेतन्याहुले भने यस्तो सरकार गठन भए इजरायलका लागि नराम्रो हुने प्रतिक्रिया दिएका छन् । इजरायलको संसद्मा अहिलेसम्म कुनै पनि राजनीतिक दलले एक्लै पूर्ण बहुमत प्राप्त गर्न सकेको छैन । त्यसैले त्यहाँ सरकार गठनका लागि विभिन्न दलबीच गठबन्धन आवश्यक पर्ने गरेको छ । नेतन्याहुको दक्षिणपन्थी लिकुड पार्टी र उसका अतिदक्षिणपन्थी तथा अति रूढिवादी यहुदी सहयोगी दलहरूले १२० सदस्यीय संसद्मा ५३ सिट जितेका छन् । त्यस्तै, आइजेनकोटको मध्यमार्गी याशर पार्टीसहित विपक्षी गठबन्धनका अन्य तीन यहुदी दलले ४८ सिट जितेका छन् । नेतन्याहुले के भने ? राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगले आइजेनकोटलाई सरकार गठनको जिम्मेवारी दिने निर्णय सार्वजनिक गर्नुभन्दा करिब एक घण्टाअघि कार्यवाहक प्रधानमन्त्री नेतन्याहुले विपक्षी दल र अरब पार्टीहरूबीच सम्भावित गठबन्धनप्रति आपत्ति जनाएका थिए । बीबीसी फारसीका अनुसार भिडियो सन्देश जारी गर्दै नेतन्याहुले अरब पार्टीहरूको समर्थनमा बन्ने सरकारले देशलाई पतनतर्फ लैजाने चेतावनी दिएका थिए । उनले भनेका थिए, ‘इस्लामवादीहरूसँग सम्बन्धित यस्तो सरकारले इसराइललाई भित्रैबाट कमजोर बनाउनेछ । युरोपेली देशहरूमा देखिएको भन्दा पनि खराब अवस्था सिर्जना हुन सक्छ ।’ सरकार गठनमा निर्णायक बन्ने अरब पार्टीहरू अरब मतदाताको उल्लेख्य सहभागितापछि अरब नेतृत्वका दुई गठबन्धन युनाइटेड अरब लिस्ट (रा’म) र जोइन्ट लिस्टले संयुक्त रूपमा १९ सिट जितेका छन् । उनीहरू अहिले सरकार गठनका लागि निर्णायक शक्तिका रूपमा देखिएका छन् । यद्यपि, यहुदी राजनीतिक दलमध्ये एउटाबाहेक अन्य सबैले निर्वाचनअघि अरब पार्टीहरूसँग मिलेर सरकार गठन नगर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएका थिए । राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगको कार्यालयले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिअनुसार सबै राजनीतिक पक्षसँग परामर्श गरेपछि आइजेनकोटलाई सरकार गठनको जिम्मेवारी दिने निर्णय गरिएको हो । राष्ट्रपतिको कार्यालयले आइजेनकोट र नेतन्याहु दुवैलाई निर्णयबारे जानकारी गराइसकेको जनाएको छ । नवनिर्वाचित सांसदहरूका प्रतिनिधिमण्डलसँगको परामर्शपछि आइजेनकोटका पक्षमा प्रधानमन्त्री बन्न ६७ र नेतन्याहुका पक्षमा ४६ सिफारिस प्राप्त भएका थिए । इजरायलको राष्ट्रपतिलाई सरकार गठनका लागि कुन नेताले सबैभन्दा बढी सम्भावना बोकेका छन् भन्ने निर्णय गर्ने अधिकार हुन्छ । त्यसैले सबैभन्दा धेरै सिट जित्ने दलका नेतालाई नै सरकार गठनको जिम्मेवारी दिनुपर्ने बाध्यता राष्ट्रपतिलाई हुँदैन । सरकार गठनका तीन सम्भावित विकल्प निर्वाचन परिणामपछि इसराइलमा सरकार गठनका लागि तीनवटा सम्भावित विकल्प देखिएका थिए । पहिलो, नेतन्याहु र आइजेनकोट दुवैलाई समेटेर राष्ट्रिय एकता सरकार गठन गर्ने । दोस्रो, नेतन्याहु र आइजेनकोटको गठबन्धनबाट अलग भएका सदस्यहरूलाई समेटेर दक्षिणपन्थी गठबन्धन बनाउने । तेस्रो, अरब पार्टीहरूको समर्थनमा आइजेनकोटको नेतृत्वमा सरकार गठन गर्ने । आइजेनकोटको गठबन्धनका एक सदस्यबाहेक अन्य सबैले यसअघि अरब पार्टीहरूसँग मिलेर सरकारमा सहभागी नहुने बताउँदै आएका थिए । यद्यपि, पछिल्लो राजनीतिक परिस्थितिमा कुनै सहमति हुन सक्ने अनुमान गरिएको छ । उनले अति रूढिवादी यहुदी दलहरूसँग पनि सहकार्यको प्रयास गर्न सक्छन् । तर त्यस्तो सहमति जुटाउन पनि कठिन हुने देखिएको छ । यसअघि पनि इजरायलमा राष्ट्रिय एकता सरकार गठन भएको उदाहरण छ । सन् २०२० मा लगातार तीनवटा निर्वाचनपछि पनि कुनै दलले स्पष्ट बहुमत प्राप्त गर्न नसकेपछि नेतन्याहु र उनका मध्यमार्गी राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धी बेनी गान्ट्जबीच सत्ता साझेदारीको सहमति भएको थियो। उक्त सहमतिअनुसार दुवैले पालैपालो सरकारको नेतृत्व गरेका थिए । राजनीतिक दलहरूसँगको छलफलका क्रममा राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगले अर्को निर्वाचन हुन नदिन र स्थिर सरकार गठन गर्न सबै दललाई लचिलो बन्न आग्रह गरेका थिए । उनले भनेका थिए, ‘अर्को निर्वाचनबाट बच्न र स्थिर सरकार गठन गर्न राजनीतिक दल तथा तिनका प्रतिनिधिहरूले वर्तमान परिस्थितिमा आफ्ना सबै वाचा र प्रतिबद्धता पूरा गर्न सम्भव नहुन सक्छ भन्ने कुरा बुझ्नुपर्छ ।’ सन् २०१९ देखि २०२२ सम्मको अवधि इसराइलको राजनीतिक इतिहासमा सबैभन्दा बढी अस्थिर र विभाजित समयमध्ये एक मानिन्छ । त्यस अवधिमा नेतन्याहु र उनका राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धीहरूबीच सरकार गठनका लागि आवश्यक सहमति जुट्न नसक्दा पाँच पटक आमनिर्वाचन भएको थियो । Kathmandu. Israeli President Isaac Herzog has decided to give opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a new coalition government. In last week's elections, neither the Eisenkot-led coalition nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition achieved the majority needed to form a government. President Herzog then held discussions with various political parties. With the president's decision, Eisenkot has 28 days to form a new government. He can be given an additional 14 days if necessary. Following the president's decision, Eisenkot wrote on social media, "Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do my best to be qualified for this." However, Prime Minister Netanyahu has responded that the formation of such a government would be bad for Israel. No political party has ever won an absolute majority in Israel's parliament, so a coalition between different parties is often required to form a government. Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-member parliament. Similarly, the three other Jewish parties in the opposition coalition, including Eisenkot's centrist Yashar Party, won 48 seats. What did Netanyahu say? About an hour before President Herzog announced his decision to give Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a government, Acting Prime Minister Netanyahu had objected to a possible alliance between the opposition and Arab parties. According to BBC Persian, in a video message, Netanyahu warned that a government formed with the support of Arab parties would lead the country to collapse. He said, "Such a government linked to Islamists would weaken Israel from within. It could create a situation worse than what is seen in European countries." Arab parties to be decisive in government formation Following a significant turnout of Arab voters, two Arab-led coalitions, the United Arab List (RAL) and the Joint List, won a combined 19 seats. They are now seen as the decisive force in forming a government. However, all but one of the Jewish political parties had pledged not to form a government with Arab parties before the election. According to a statement issued by President Herzog's office, the decision to give Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a government was made after consulting with all political parties. The presidential office said it had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision. After consultations with a delegation of newly elected MPs, 67 recommendations were received in favor of Eisenkot becoming prime minister and 46 in favor of Netanyahu. The President of Israel has the authority to decide which leader has the best chance of forming a government. Therefore, the President is not obligated to give the responsibility of forming a government to the leader of the party that wins the most seats. Three possible options for government formation Following the election results, three possible options emerged for forming a government in Israel. First, to form a national unity government including both Netanyahu and Eisenkot. Second, to form a right-wing coalition by including members who broke away from Netanyahu and Eisenkot's coalition. Third, to form a government led by Eisenkot with the support of Arab parties. All but one member of Eisenkot's coalition had previously said they would not join a government with Arab parties, although there is speculation that an agreement could be reached in the current political climate. He may also try to cooperate with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties, but even that consensus appears to be difficult to achieve. There has been an example of a national unity government in Israel before. In 2020, after three consecutive elections, no party could win a clear majority, Netanyahu and his centrist political rival Benny Gantz reached a power-sharing agreement. Under the agreement, the two took turns leading the government. During discussions with political parties, President Herzog urged all parties to be flexible in order to avoid another election and form a stable government. He said, "To avoid another election and form a stable government, political parties and their representatives must understand that it may not be possible to fulfill all their promises and commitments in the current situation." The period from 2019 to 2022 is considered one of the most volatile and divisive in Israel's political history. During that period, five general elections were held as Netanyahu and his political rivals failed to reach the necessary agreement to form a government.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog has decided to give opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a new coalition government. In last week's elections, neither the Eisenkot-led coalition nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition achieved the majority needed to form a government. President Herzog then held discussions with various political parties. With the president's decision, Eisenkot has 28 days to form a new government. He can be given an additional 14 days if necessary. Following the president's decision, Eisenkot wrote on social media, "Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do my best to be qualified for this." However, Prime Minister Netanyahu has responded that the formation of such a government would be bad for Israel. No political party has ever won an absolute majority in Israel's parliament, so a coalition between different parties is often required to form a government. Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-member parliament. Similarly, the three other Jewish parties in the opposition coalition, including Eisenkot's centrist Yashar Party, won 48 seats. What did Netanyahu say? About an hour before President Herzog announced his decision to give Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a government, Acting Prime Minister Netanyahu had objected to a possible alliance between the opposition and Arab parties. According to BBC Persian, in a video message, Netanyahu warned that a government formed with the support of Arab parties would lead the country to collapse. He said, "Such a government linked to Islamists would weaken Israel from within. It could create a situation worse than what is seen in European countries." Arab parties to be decisive in government formation Following a significant turnout of Arab voters, two Arab-led coalitions, the United Arab List (RAL) and the Joint List, won a combined 19 seats. They are now seen as the decisive force in forming a government. However, all but one of the Jewish political parties had pledged not to form a government with Arab parties before the election. According to a statement issued by President Herzog's office, the decision to give Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a government was made after consulting with all political parties. The presidential office said it had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision. After consultations with a delegation of newly elected MPs, 67 recommendations were received in favor of Eisenkot becoming prime minister and 46 in favor of Netanyahu. The President of Israel has the authority to decide which leader has the best chance of forming a government. Therefore, the President is not obligated to give the responsibility of forming a government to the leader of the party that wins the most seats. Three possible options for government formation Following the election results, three possible options emerged for forming a government in Israel. First, to form a national unity government including both Netanyahu and Eisenkot. Second, to form a right-wing coalition by including members who broke away from Netanyahu and Eisenkot's coalition. Third, to form a government led by Eisenkot with the support of Arab parties. All but one member of Eisenkot's coalition had previously said they would not join a government with Arab parties, although there is speculation that an agreement could be reached in the current political climate. He may also try to cooperate with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties, but even that consensus appears to be difficult to achieve. There has been an example of a national unity government in Israel before. In 2020, after three consecutive elections, no party could win a clear majority, Netanyahu and his centrist political rival Benny Gantz reached a power-sharing agreement. Under the agreement, the two took turns leading the government. During discussions with political parties, President Herzog urged all parties to be flexible in order to avoid another election and form a stable government. He said, "To avoid another election and form a stable government, political parties and their representatives must understand that it may not be possible to fulfill all their promises and commitments in the current situation." The period from 2019 to 2022 is considered one of the most volatile and divisive in Israel's political history. During that period, five general elections were held as Netanyahu and his political rivals failed to reach the necessary agreement to form a government.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog has decided to give opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a new coalition government. In last week's elections, neither the Eisenkot-led coalition nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition achieved the majority needed to form a government. President Herzog then held discussions with various political parties. With the president's decision, Eisenkot has 28 days to form a new government. He can be given an additional 14 days if necessary. Following the president's decision, Eisenkot wrote on social media, "Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do my best to be qualified for this." However, Prime Minister Netanyahu has responded that the formation of such a government would be bad for Israel. No political party has ever won an absolute majority in Israel's parliament, so a coalition between different parties is often required to form a government. Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-member parliament. Similarly, the three other Jewish parties in the opposition coalition, including Eisenkot's centrist Yashar Party, won 48 seats. What did Netanyahu say? About an hour before President Herzog announced his decision to give Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a government, Acting Prime Minister Netanyahu had objected to a possible alliance between the opposition and Arab parties. According to BBC Persian, in a video message, Netanyahu warned that a government formed with the support of Arab parties would lead the country to collapse. He said, "Such a government linked to Islamists would weaken Israel from within. It could create a situation worse than what is seen in European countries." Arab parties to be decisive in government formation Following a significant turnout of Arab voters, two Arab-led coalitions, the United Arab List (RAL) and the Joint List, won a combined 19 seats. They are now seen as the decisive force in forming a government. However, all but one of the Jewish political parties had pledged not to form a government with Arab parties before the election. According to a statement issued by President Herzog's office, the decision to give Eisenkot the responsibility of forming a government was made after consulting with all political parties. The presidential office said it had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision. After consultations with a delegation of newly elected MPs, 67 recommendations were received in favor of Eisenkot becoming prime minister and 46 in favor of Netanyahu. The President of Israel has the authority to decide which leader has the best chance of forming a government. Therefore, the President is not obligated to give the responsibility of forming a government to the leader of the party that wins the most seats. Three possible options for government formation Following the election results, three possible options emerged for forming a government in Israel. First, to form a national unity government including both Netanyahu and Eisenkot. Second, to form a right-wing coalition by including members who broke away from Netanyahu and Eisenkot's coalition. Third, to form a government led by Eisenkot with the support of Arab parties. All but one member of Eisenkot's coalition had previously said they would not join a government with Arab parties, although there is speculation that an agreement could be reached in the current political climate. He may also try to cooperate with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties, but even that consensus appears to be difficult to achieve. There has been an example of a national unity government in Israel before. In 2020, after three consecutive elections, no party could win a clear majority, Netanyahu and his centrist political rival Benny Gantz reached a power-sharing agreement. Under the agreement, the two took turns leading the government. During discussions with political parties, President Herzog urged all parties to be flexible in order to avoid another election and form a stable government. He said, "To avoid another election and form a stable government, political parties and their representatives must understand that it may not be possible to fulfill all their promises and commitments in the current situation." The period from 2019 to 2022 is considered one of the most volatile and divisive in Israel's political history. During that period, five general elections were held as Netanyahu and his political rivals failed to reach the necessary agreement to form a government.

गठनका लागि तीनवटा सम्भावित विकल्प देखिएका थिए । पहिलो, नेतन्याहु र आइजेनकोट दुवैलाई समेटेर राष्ट्रिय एकता सरकार गठन गर्ने । दोस्रो, नेतन्याहु र आइजेनकोटको गठबन्धनबाट अलग भएका सदस्यहरूलाई समेटेर दक्षिणपन्थी गठबन्धन बनाउने । तेस्रो, अरब पार्टीहरूको समर्थनमा आइजेनकोटको नेतृत्वमा सरकार गठन गर्ने । आइजेनकोटको गठबन्धनका एक सदस्यबाहेक अन्य सबैले यसअघि अरब पार्टीहरूसँग मिलेर सरकारमा सहभागी नहुने बताउँदै आएका थिए । यद्यपि, पछिल्लो राजनीतिक परिस्थितिमा कुनै सहमति हुन सक्ने अनुमान गरिएको छ । उनले अति रूढिवादी यहुदी दलहरूसँग पनि सहकार्यको प्रयास गर्न सक्छन् । तर त्यस्तो सहमति जुटाउन पनि कठिन हुने देखिएको छ । यसअघि पनि इजरायलमा राष्ट्रिय एकता सरकार गठन भएको उदाहरण छ । सन् २०२० मा लगातार तीनवटा निर्वाचनपछि पनि कुनै दलले स्पष्ट बहुमत प्राप्त गर्न नसकेपछि नेतन्याहु र उनका मध्यमार्गी राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धी बेनी गान्ट्जबीच सत्ता साझेदारीको सहमति भएको थियो। उक्त सहमतिअनुसार दुवैले पालैपालो सरकारको नेतृत्व गरेका थिए । राजनीतिक दलहरूसँगको छलफलका क्रममा राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगले अर्को निर्वाचन हुन नदिन र स्थिर सरकार गठन गर्न सबै दललाई लचिलो बन्न आग्रह गरेका थिए । उनले भनेका थिए, ‘अर्को निर्वाचनबाट बच्न र स्थिर सरकार गठन गर्न राजनीतिक दल तथा तिनका प्रतिनिधिहरूले वर्तमान परिस्थितिमा आफ्ना सबै वाचा र प्रतिबद्धता पूरा गर्न सम्भव नहुन सक्छ भन्ने कुरा बुझ्नुपर्छ ।’ सन् २०१९ देखि २०२२ सम्मको अवधि इसराइलको राजनीतिक इतिहासमा सबैभन्दा बढी अस्थिर र विभाजित समयमध्ये एक मानिन्छ । त्यस अवधिमा नेतन्याहु र उनका राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धीहरूबीच सरकार गठनका लागि आवश्यक सहमति जुट्न नसक्दा पाँच पटक आमनिर्वाचन भएको थियो ।

काठमाडौं । इजरायलका राष्ट्रपति इसाक हर्जोगले विपक्षी नेता गादी आइजेनकोटलाई नयाँ गठबन्धन सरकार गठन गर्ने जिम्मेवारी दिने निर्णय गरेका छन् ।

गत साता सम्पन्न निर्वाचनमा न त आइजेनकोट नेतृत्वको गठबन्धनले न त प्रधानमन्त्री बेन्जामिन नेतन्याहुको गठबन्धनले सरकार गठनका लागि आवश्यक बहुमत प्राप्त गर्न सके ।

त्यसपछि राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगले विभिन्न राजनीतिक दलसँग छलफल गरेका थिए ।

राष्ट्रपतिको निर्णयसँगै आइजेनकोटले नयाँ सरकार गठनका लागि २८ दिनको समय पाएका छन् । आवश्यक परे उनलाई थप १४ दिन समय दिन सकिनेछ ।

राष्ट्रपतिको निर्णयपछि आइजेनकोटले सामाजिक सञ्जाल एक्समा लेखेका छन्, ‘अब राष्ट्रिय आपत्कालीन सरकार गठन गर्ने समय आएको छ । यसका लागि योग्य बन्न म सक्दो प्रयास गर्नेछु ।’

तर, प्रधानमन्त्री नेतन्याहुले भने यस्तो सरकार गठन भए इजरायलका लागि नराम्रो हुने प्रतिक्रिया दिएका छन् ।

इजरायलको संसद्मा अहिलेसम्म कुनै पनि राजनीतिक दलले एक्लै पूर्ण बहुमत प्राप्त गर्न सकेको छैन । त्यसैले त्यहाँ सरकार गठनका लागि विभिन्न दलबीच गठबन्धन आवश्यक पर्ने गरेको छ ।

नेतन्याहुको दक्षिणपन्थी लिकुड पार्टी र उसका अतिदक्षिणपन्थी तथा अति रूढिवादी यहुदी सहयोगी दलहरूले १२० सदस्यीय संसद्मा ५३ सिट जितेका छन् । त्यस्तै, आइजेनकोटको मध्यमार्गी याशर पार्टीसहित विपक्षी गठबन्धनका अन्य तीन यहुदी दलले ४८ सिट जितेका छन् ।

नेतन्याहुले के भने ?

राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगले आइजेनकोटलाई सरकार गठनको जिम्मेवारी दिने निर्णय सार्वजनिक गर्नुभन्दा करिब एक घण्टाअघि कार्यवाहक प्रधानमन्त्री नेतन्याहुले विपक्षी दल र अरब पार्टीहरूबीच सम्भावित गठबन्धनप्रति आपत्ति जनाएका थिए ।

बीबीसी फारसीका अनुसार भिडियो सन्देश जारी गर्दै नेतन्याहुले अरब पार्टीहरूको समर्थनमा बन्ने सरकारले देशलाई पतनतर्फ लैजाने चेतावनी दिएका थिए ।

उनले भनेका थिए, ‘इस्लामवादीहरूसँग सम्बन्धित यस्तो सरकारले इसराइललाई भित्रैबाट कमजोर बनाउनेछ । युरोपेली देशहरूमा देखिएको भन्दा पनि खराब अवस्था सिर्जना हुन सक्छ ।’

सरकार गठनमा निर्णायक बन्ने अरब पार्टीहरू

अरब मतदाताको उल्लेख्य सहभागितापछि अरब नेतृत्वका दुई गठबन्धन युनाइटेड अरब लिस्ट (रा’म) र जोइन्ट लिस्टले संयुक्त रूपमा १९ सिट जितेका छन् । उनीहरू अहिले सरकार गठनका लागि निर्णायक शक्तिका रूपमा देखिएका छन् ।

यद्यपि, यहुदी राजनीतिक दलमध्ये एउटाबाहेक अन्य सबैले निर्वाचनअघि अरब पार्टीहरूसँग मिलेर सरकार गठन नगर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएका थिए ।

राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगको कार्यालयले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिअनुसार सबै राजनीतिक पक्षसँग परामर्श गरेपछि आइजेनकोटलाई सरकार गठनको जिम्मेवारी दिने निर्णय गरिएको हो ।

राष्ट्रपतिको कार्यालयले आइजेनकोट र नेतन्याहु दुवैलाई निर्णयबारे जानकारी गराइसकेको जनाएको छ ।

नवनिर्वाचित सांसदहरूका प्रतिनिधिमण्डलसँगको परामर्शपछि आइजेनकोटका पक्षमा प्रधानमन्त्री बन्न ६७ र नेतन्याहुका पक्षमा ४६ सिफारिस प्राप्त भएका थिए ।

इजरायलको राष्ट्रपतिलाई सरकार गठनका लागि कुन नेताले सबैभन्दा बढी सम्भावना बोकेका छन् भन्ने निर्णय गर्ने अधिकार हुन्छ । त्यसैले सबैभन्दा धेरै सिट जित्ने दलका नेतालाई नै सरकार गठनको जिम्मेवारी दिनुपर्ने बाध्यता राष्ट्रपतिलाई हुँदैन ।

सरकार गठनका तीन सम्भावित विकल्प

निर्वाचन परिणामपछि इसराइलमा सरकार गठनका लागि तीनवटा सम्भावित विकल्प देखिएका थिए ।

पहिलो, नेतन्याहु र आइजेनकोट दुवैलाई समेटेर राष्ट्रिय एकता सरकार गठन गर्ने ।

दोस्रो, नेतन्याहु र आइजेनकोटको गठबन्धनबाट अलग भएका सदस्यहरूलाई समेटेर दक्षिणपन्थी गठबन्धन बनाउने ।

तेस्रो, अरब पार्टीहरूको समर्थनमा आइजेनकोटको नेतृत्वमा सरकार गठन गर्ने ।

आइजेनकोटको गठबन्धनका एक सदस्यबाहेक अन्य सबैले यसअघि अरब पार्टीहरूसँग मिलेर सरकारमा सहभागी नहुने बताउँदै आएका थिए । यद्यपि, पछिल्लो राजनीतिक परिस्थितिमा कुनै सहमति हुन सक्ने अनुमान गरिएको छ ।

उनले अति रूढिवादी यहुदी दलहरूसँग पनि सहकार्यको प्रयास गर्न सक्छन् । तर त्यस्तो सहमति जुटाउन पनि कठिन हुने देखिएको छ ।

यसअघि पनि इजरायलमा राष्ट्रिय एकता सरकार गठन भएको उदाहरण छ । सन् २०२० मा लगातार तीनवटा निर्वाचनपछि पनि कुनै दलले स्पष्ट बहुमत प्राप्त गर्न नसकेपछि नेतन्याहु र उनका मध्यमार्गी राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धी बेनी गान्ट्जबीच सत्ता साझेदारीको सहमति भएको थियो। उक्त सहमतिअनुसार दुवैले पालैपालो सरकारको नेतृत्व गरेका थिए ।

राजनीतिक दलहरूसँगको छलफलका क्रममा राष्ट्रपति हर्जोगले अर्को निर्वाचन हुन नदिन र स्थिर सरकार गठन गर्न सबै दललाई लचिलो बन्न आग्रह गरेका थिए ।

The President of Israel has the authority to decide which leader has the best chance of forming a government. Therefore, the President is not obligated to give the responsibility of forming a government to the leader of the party that wins the most seats.

Three possible options for government formation

Following the election results, three possible options emerged for forming a government in Israel.

First, to form a national unity government including both Netanyahu and Eisenkot.

Second, to form a right-wing coalition by including members who broke away from Netanyahu and Eisenkot's coalition.

Third, to form a government led by Eisenkot with the support of Arab parties.

All but one member of Eisenkot's coalition had previously said they would not join a government with Arab parties, although there is speculation that an agreement could be reached in the current political climate.

He may also try to cooperate with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties, but even that consensus appears to be difficult to achieve.

There has been an example of a national unity government in Israel before. In 2020, after three consecutive elections, no party could win a clear majority, Netanyahu and his centrist political rival Benny Gantz reached a power-sharing agreement. Under the agreement, the two took turns leading the government.

During discussions with political parties, President Herzog urged all parties to be flexible in order to avoid another election and form a stable government.

He said, "To avoid another election and form a stable government, political parties and their representatives must understand that it may not be possible to fulfill all their promises and commitments in the current situation."

The period from 2019 to 2022 is considered one of the most volatile and divisive in Israel's political history. During that period, five general elections were held as Netanyahu and his political rivals failed to reach the necessary agreement to form a government.
